findings.finding: Deliverable 5's gate text in docs/releases/v2.0.0-plugin-transformation-requirements.md SS 9 ('Installs and uninstalls cleanly on Windows') is measured-false by FR-14a item 4 (plugin_schema_spike.md): claude plugin uninstall leaves two settings.json keys emptied but not removed, plus an orphaned, unpruned plugin-cache directory. This is the same defect as FR-18's now-unachievable AC one level up and needs a synchronized rewrite by the same owner, business-analyst-agent, not a second independent decision.

NFR-2 was under-scoped in the Phase 0 draft by being bundled into a shared 3-point 'measurement harness' row with NFR-1. ADR-016 shows it requires a 5-mechanism resilience-engineering build across 6 timeout= call sites in 5 files, including a 75-second wall-clock abort on the pipeline's own critical path (task_orchestration.py:160/217). Re-scored to size 8, WSJF 2.88, as its own row. If this re-scope is not carried into planning, D6 cannot close on NFR-2 as originally estimated.

FR-23's MUST-PRECEDE-FR-4 ordering constraint, which protects the version-push gate closed by commit 1bb4303, is specified in ADR-017 but has no CI enforcement as of this revision. An out-of-order merge deleting hooks/pre_tool_enforcer/ before the MCP port lands would silently reopen a bypass someone explicitly closed, with no failing test to catch it. This is now the top unresolved sequencing risk, tied with FR-9a's build-completeness risk.

NFR-3 was overscored (size 8, WSJF 3.00) against a false premise that a new crash-recovery writer had to be built. HLD OAQ 1 shows CheckpointManager already exists, already wired at every step boundary, and survives FR-4 untouched. Re-scored to size 3, WSJF 6.33 -- this frees planning capacity inside D6 and should be sequenced early, alongside the other cheap high-WSJF governance fixes (FR-22, FR-6), rather than left at its old implied low priority.

FR-4/FR-5's WSJF row carried a 'core NFR-1 outcome' justification partly resting on an assumed large process-footprint reduction. ADR-018's corrected spawn-site census shows FR-4+FR-5 remove roughly 6 of 116 spawn sites (~5%); the real value is invocation-frequency reduction (2 interpreter starts per tool call), not footprint. Re-scored UBV 9->8, CoD 21->20, WSJF 7.00->6.67, and the row's framing corrected to 'necessary but not sufficient for NFR-1' given ADR-018's bundled-MCP-server finding.

FR-18's AC is unachievable as written against measured claude plugin uninstall behaviour (empty-but-present settings.json keys, orphaned unpruned cache directory). business-analyst-agent owns the rewrite; both plausible resolution paths are sized here (FR-18a plugin-shipped cleanup command, +2 points/WSJF 6.50, versus AC-narrowing to plugin-attributable residue only, no size delta) so D5 is ready whichever way it lands.

The NFR-1/bundled-MCP-server conflict (ADR-018 item 5, measured: 2 confirmed spawns in a session that forbade tool use) was entirely unsized in the prior revision. It is assigned to solution-architect for decision at Phase 2.3, not decided here. Three options are sized: (a) bundle zero MCP servers (~5 pts, breaks FR-14's one-step-install AC, does NOT preserve the MVP boundary), (b) redefine NFR-1 to name a minimum-viable bundled set matching the HLD's existing ADR-018 design (~1 pt, DOES preserve the MVP boundary), (c) per-server lazy opt-in (~8+ pts, unproven platform capability per the spike, does NOT preserve the MVP boundary as currently scoped).

phase_2_3_amendment.decision: ADR-019: the plugin is designed to bundle ZERO MCP servers. Registration is designed as an explicit opt-in `register-mcp` command (the user would run it once, by choice) -- PROPOSED, no code exists yet; `unregister-mcp` is designed to reverse it -- also PROPOSED, not built. Decisive reasoning accepted without dispute: NFR-1 already took one carve-out (the retained Stop hook, via per-component attribution); a second carve-out for bundled MCP would leave nothing capable of making NFR-1 fail, and a metric that cannot fail measures nothing. This is a measurement-falsifiability argument WSJF has no term for, not a WSJF override.
phase_2_3_amendment.mvp_boundary_verdict: Does NOT move to v2.1. Composition changed, not boundary: the register-mcp/unregister-mcp command pair (PROPOSED by ADR-019, not yet built) is new, MANDATORY v2.0.0 scope (there is no bundle-instead fallback to defer under option (a)). What genuinely changed is that an implicit property of the boundary -- one-step install of the COMPLETE capability set -- silently carried inside FR-14's original wording and D5's gate text, was never itself a named boundary line item, and has now failed for the MCP-backed half. This document now names it explicitly (one-step install is designed to cover commands/agents/skills only; MCP-backed capabilities are designed to require the separate register-mcp step, once built) rather than leaving the loss implicit a second time.

register_mcp_sizing.reference_implementation: Reinertsen (2009) WSJF = CoD/size, CoD = UBV+TC+RROE, via product-management-core/SKILL.md -- same instrument as every other row in this document
register_mcp_sizing.reasoning: UBV=7: would be the sole path to any MCP-backed capability under option (a), including the FR-23 push gate, once built. TC=6, not higher: does not block D6's actual gate, because FR-23 ordering is DESIGNED to be CI-enforced via ADR-017 (that CI assertion is itself PROPOSED, not yet wired -- see critical_path.sequence) independent of whether register-mcp is ever run; it does block FR-14a/NFR-5's install-test AC and the ADR-019 discoverability requirement. RROE=6: would close a real correctness/UX gap (silent absence of a capability presenting as working) and would add NFR-5's 4th test scenario, but is new-feature work, not a defect fix, scoring below NFR-3's re-scored defect-fix row (6.33). Size=5: comparable to FR-7's slash-command entry-point row -- two new commands, a shared settings.json write-safety helper two writers would need to use consistently (flagged in advisory_items.json as sharpened, ESCALATION CANDIDATE), one new round-trip test.

fr18a_disposition.same_row_or_distinct: SAME ROW resurfacing, not a distinct one. This is SS 2a's FR-18a (plugin-shipped cleanup command, D5, size 2, WSJF 6.50), previously retired once already (housekeeping_correction_found_incidentally above, and SS 2c in the amended document) as 'not-activated' -- i.e., framed as a road BA chose not to take. That framing was incomplete: FR-18a was never a buildable road, independent of any BA choice.
fr18a_disposition.why_invalid: The residue FR-18a was sized to clean (two settings.json bookkeeping keys emptied to {} but not removed, an orphaned plugin-cache directory claude plugin prune does not clean) comes into existence at the moment claude plugin uninstall completes -- exactly when the plugin's own code stops running. A plugin-shipped command has no execution point after that instant: no uninstall-time hook, no post-uninstall callback exists for a plugin to register. Structurally identical to HLD ADR-020's Path C finding: once the plugin is gone, no plugin code runs, so neither prevention nor detection is available to it. FR-18a as scoped names a contradiction, not a deprioritized capability.
fr18a_disposition.disposition: FOLD INTO FR-24 (option b). Option (a), pre-uninstall preparation, was checked and NOT adopted: the plugin's only pre-uninstall-reachable state is its own MCP registrations, and unregister-mcp -- PROPOSED by ADR-019, not built (sized in phase_2_3_amendment.register_mcp_sizing, size 5/WSJF 3.80) -- is designed to reach those in full, once it exists. The remaining residue (the two bookkeeping keys, the orphaned cache directory) is written and owned entirely by Claude Code's own uninstall/caching machinery -- no pre-uninstall plugin action changes it. Sizing FR-18a as (a) would size a command whose entire effective scope would duplicate unregister-mcp's designed scope. FR-24 (docs/guides/uninstall-residue.md -- NAMED by business-analyst-agent at Phase 2.1 with a defined AC, status 'Named at Phase 2.1; not started' per prd-v2.md; the file does not exist on disk, verified) is the shape that would actually work, because a human would run it after the plugin is gone -- the only time the residue exists and the only actor left who could act on it. FR-18a's original intent is fully subsumed by FR-24's already-defined (not yet built) scope.
fr18a_disposition.size_reasoning: Per the reference implementation (Reinertsen 2009, WSJF = CoD/size, via product-management-core/SKILL.md), a contingency that resolves to no independent work has no CoD left to score -- the capability falls fully within FR-24's already-defined-but-not-yet-built scope, and the only genuine pre-uninstall opportunity falls fully within unregister-mcp's already-defined-but-not-yet-built scope. Retired at an honest zero, not carried forward at 6.50 or re-priced at a smaller nonzero figure to appear conservative. This zero is a scoping conclusion (no independent unit of work exists to size once FR-24 and unregister-mcp are built as designed), not a claim that either is currently complete.
